title: The total Cech complex of a bounded complex of flat sheaves is K-flat

standard_prerequisites.name: In a distinguished triangle, if two of the three objects are K-flat complexes of modules then so is the third
standard_prerequisites.use: Runs the induction on the width of the bounded complex down to a single sheaf.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Cech complex of a covering agrees up to homotopy equivalence with the alternating Cech complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Passes from the total Cech complex to the alternating one whose terms are sections over the intersections.

standard_prerequisites.name: A bounded complex of flat modules is K-flat
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes the proof once the terms are seen to be A-flat.

core_obligations: Write F^bullet = (F^a to ... to F^b) and induct on b - a using the distinguished triangle F^b[-b] to (F^a to ... to F^b) to (F^a to ... to F^{b-1}) to F^b[-b+1] together with More on Algebra, Lemma K-flat-two-out-of-three to reduce to the case of a single quasi-coherent O_X-module F in degree 0 (proof lines 5914-5925).
In the single-sheaf case, the Cech complex for F and the covering U is homotopy equivalent to the alternating Cech complex by Cohomology, Lemma alternating-usual (proof lines 5926-5931).

Conclude: since every intersection U_{i_0...i_p} is affine, the module of sections F(U_{i_0...i_p}) is A-flat; hence the alternating Cech complex is a bounded complex of flat A-modules and therefore K-flat by More on Algebra, Lemma derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism, which gives the claim for Tot(C^bullet(U, F^bullet)) (proof lines 5931-5940).
proof_roadmap: Induct on the width of the complex via the triangle and two-out-of-three for K-flatness (proof lines 5914-5925).
Replace the Cech complex by the alternating Cech complex up to homotopy (proof lines 5926-5931).
Use affinity of the intersections for flatness of the terms and K-flatness of bounded flat complexes (proof lines 5931-5940).
